context: The input is the four-element array [7,3,2,6], with indices 0 through 3. Recursively process the left half first, then the right half, and finally merge the two sorted results.
description: The figure retains subproblems already expanded and results already returned to show the history of recursive calls. These are snapshots at different times, not multiple current versions of the array. A subarray of length 1 returns immediately.

The “Merge sort calls and returns” table below lists ten records by the step in which they first appear. The full history at step N consists of the records first shown in steps 1 through N. Returned results do not overwrite the input snapshots in the table. To merge, compare the first remaining element from each side and take the smaller one. When one side runs out, append the remainder from the other. The ten steps count illustrated states, not element comparisons.

frames.announcement: Start the top-level merge sort with input [7, 3, 2, 6].
frames.explanation: Start the top-level merge sort on [7, 3, 2, 6]. Neither subproblem has been expanded. For the full history shown, see the record first appearing in step 1 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The top-level input is [7, 3, 2, 6]. Neither subproblem has been expanded.
frames.title: Start sorting four elements

frames.explanation: Following the left-before-right order, enter the left half [7, 3]. The right half [2, 6] has yet to be expanded. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 2 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left half [7, 3] is being processed. The right half [2, 6] has yet to be expanded.
frames.title: Recursively process the left half

frames.announcement: Enter the single-element array [7] and return immediately.
frames.explanation: Split the left half [7, 3] and enter [7] first. It returns immediately because its length is 1. Neither [3] nor the right half has been expanded. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 3 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: On the left, [7] has returned. Neither [3] nor the right half has been expanded.
frames.title: Split off the single element 7 on the left

frames.announcement: Enter the single-element array [3] and return immediately.
frames.explanation: After [7] returns, enter [3] and return immediately. Both single elements on the left are ready to merge. The right half has yet to be expanded. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 4 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: Both [7] and [3] on the left have returned and await merging. The right half has yet to be expanded.
frames.title: Split off the single element 3 on the left

frames.announcement: The left merge is complete and returns [3, 7].
frames.explanation: Compare the returned arrays [7] and [3] on the left, merge them into [3, 7], and return. The right half has yet to be expanded. The figure retains [7, 3] as a snapshot of the input to the call. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 5 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left half has returned [3, 7]. The right half has yet to be expanded.
frames.title: Merge the left half into [3,7]

frames.announcement: The left half is complete. Enter the right half [2, 6].
frames.explanation: The left half has returned the sorted result [3, 7]. Now enter the right half [2, 6]. Its two single-element subproblems have yet to be expanded. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 6 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left half has returned [3, 7]. Enter the right half [2, 6], whose single-element subproblems have yet to be expanded.
frames.title: Recursively process the right half

frames.announcement: Enter the single-element array [2] and return immediately.
frames.explanation: The left half has returned the sorted result [3, 7]. Split the right half [2, 6], enter [2] first, and return immediately. The call for [6] has yet to be expanded. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 7 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left half has returned [3, 7]. On the right, [2] has returned, and [6] has yet to be expanded.
frames.title: Split off the single element 2 on the right

frames.announcement: Enter the single-element array [6] and return immediately.
frames.explanation: After [2] returns on the right, enter [6] and return immediately. Both single elements on the right are ready to merge. The left result remains [3, 7]. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 8 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left half has returned [3, 7]. On the right, both [2] and [6] have returned and await merging.
frames.title: Split off the single element 6 on the right

frames.announcement: The right merge is complete and returns [2, 6].
frames.explanation: Merge the returned arrays [2] and [6] into [2, 6]. The left result [3, 7] and right result [2, 6] are ready for the top-level merge. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 9 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The left and right results [3, 7] and [2, 6] are ready for the top-level merge.
frames.title: Merge the right half into [2,6]

frames.announcement: The top-level merge is complete. The final array is [2, 3, 6, 7].
frames.explanation: At the top level, compare the first remaining elements of [3, 7] and [2, 6]. Take 2, then 3, then 6. The right half is exhausted, so append 7 from the left. The final result is [2, 3, 6, 7], completing the sort. The figure retains every input snapshot and returned result. For the full history shown, see the records first appearing in steps 1 through 10 in “Merge sort calls and returns.”
frames.key_state: The top-level merge is complete. The final array is [2, 3, 6, 7].
frames.title: Merge the left and right halves

summary: First sort the left half [7,3] into [3,7], then process the right half [2,6], and finally merge them into [2,3,6,7].
